reason: The ground needs a stable footing for the replacement support, and the excavator can prepare it.
expectation: The excavator will prepare level ground for the support.

effect: The excavator exposed firm ground without disturbing the loaded cribbing; the footing can now be built there.
reaction: The separation from the loaded supports makes the preparation feel sensible.
reason: Steel is the available structural material for a footing on the prepared ground.
expectation: The steel will form a broad footing or base for the replacement support.

effect: The prepared ground now carries a braced replacement support, ready to attach to the lander.
reaction: The broad plates and ceramic footing make the load path clear.
reason: The replacement leg matches the lander's sound joints, so it should fit at the tilted lander.
expectation: The new support will be fitted to the lander and help restore a level platform.

effect: The replacement support is installed and carrying the lander, completing the level launch platform.
reaction: The careful transfer of weight and the straight ladder make the repair feel tangible.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the replacement support was most worthwhile: the broad plates and ceramic blocks made its load path understandable, and fitting it resolved the temporary repair.

leastWorthwhile.text: Preparing the ground was a predictable preliminary step, though its separation from the loaded cribbing had a clear safety purpose.

surprise.text: The completed leg will stay on Mars when the upper cabin lifts away; I had not expected that detail of the return arrangement.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; each action had a clear role in preparing, building or installing the support.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how the return and the investigation of the cores unfold, particularly after this physically grounded repair.
